meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Why does my son have a zero?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Nobody called me, and Owen found out from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of a class. What was the basis for the zero, Hale?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

I'm writing down the times. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so turn the screen and show me the history itself, with the account it's under. Edits arriving in a block don't tell me who was typing, Hale.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

I'm searching the scene now, and I'm writing down that you gave me the act and scene. A line that isn't in the play is a mistake in an essay, Hale, and it doesn't tell me who made it. Did anyone speak to Owen about it before that zero went in?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
Okay. Whatever happens Thursday, nothing goes on his record and not a word reaches his class, and I want that in writing. Does the zero sit in the gradebook until then?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You told me the zero went in before you called me and that was wrong, and you offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room with the vice-principal, which I have not accepted. I still require written confirmation that nothing goes on Owen's record and nothing reaches his class, and an answer on whether the zero stays in the gradebook until then. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the fallback position. She did not accept the rewrite, and she still wants it in writing that nothing goes on his record and nothing reaches his class, plus an answer on whether the zero stays in the gradebook.
What moved her: "that was wrong. I'm sorry." Owning the zero in one sentence, before she asked, got you a flat okay and kept her from digging in at the start.
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when she asked whether anyone had spoken to Owen before the zero, you went straight to the rewrite, so answer that question directly before offering terms.
